item.text: {"classifications":[{"segment_id":"1","code":1,"rationale":"The President makes a policy finding about anticipated benefits; it supports discretionary executive management but does not itself change legal rights or duties.","evidence":"I have determined that an on-the-job safety belt use policy for Federal employees will reduce human pain and suffering"},{"segment_id":"2","code":4,"rationale":"The segment inseparably combines a presently binding duty imposed directly on federal employees (Code 3) with mandates for agencies to promulgate implementing rules and measures later (Code 2).","evidence":"Each Federal employee occupying the front seat of a motor vehicle on official business, whose seat is equipped with a safety belt, shall have the safety belt properly fastened"},{"segment_id":"3","code":1,"rationale":"The Secretary of Labor must coordinate, encourage voluntary adoption by other branches, and report annually; these are administrative and reporting functions without a dictated legal consequence.","evidence":"The Secretary of Labor shall also submit an annual report to the President"},{"segment_id":"4","code":1,"rationale":"The segment assigns coordination and implementation responsibilities while preserving existing statutory powers, rights, procedures, causes of action, and liability; it does not itself alter substantive legal consequences.","evidence":"The Secretary of Defense shall be responsible for implementation of all provisions of this Order"}]}
